title: LTS channel in Console — customer UX notes (version pinning, warnings, release notes, rollout controls)
content:
Context
- We are introducing a Runtime LTS channel for enterprise (Dedicated + Private first; Hosted later/limited).
- Console needs to make LTS discoverable without confusing it with “Latest”. Primary customer value is stability and predictable patch cadence.
- Console should reduce support load by: (1) making pinning/rollback obvious, (2) surfacing release notes + known issues, (3) warning users before switching tracks.

Non-goals for initial Console changes
- We are not building a full “runtime fleet manager” UI in v1.
- We are not exposing every internal kernel/scheduler knob. LTS implies fewer toggles.

User types / jobs-to-be-done
1) Enterprise platform engineer (Dedicated)
- Wants to pin runtime version to an LTS patch, keep it stable, and have a controlled rollout window.
- Needs to quickly answer “what changed”, “is this patch mandatory”, and “how do I roll back”.

2) Regulated ops / compliance (Private)
- Needs auditability: artifact provenance/checksums/SBOM links, and a clean mapping from “running version” -> “release notes” -> “commit/artifact metadata”.

3) Redwood Support / CS
- Needs to tell what version the customer is on, whether they’re on LTS vs Latest, whether an upgrade is recommended/required, and whether a known issue applies.

Guiding principles
- Be explicit about track: LTS vs Latest (or “Standard”) and the consequences.
- Make safe defaults easy: if you choose LTS, default to newest LTS patch in that LTS line (e.g., 1.18.x-lts), but do not auto-upgrade without consent.
- Prevent accidental churn: switching tracks and changing pinned versions should require a confirmation step with warnings.
- Always provide a release-notes link wherever a version is shown.
- Minimize “mystery tags”: display both marketing version (1.18.1-lts) and underlying runtime build identifier (commit SHA / build id) where it helps enterprise.

Terminology proposal (still open)
- Track label options:
  - Option A: “LTS” and “Latest”
  - Option B: “LTS (stable)” and “Standard (rapid)”
  - Option C: “Long Term Support” and “Current”
- Preference from Product: Option B in UI copy, but keep “LTS” as the concise badge.
- In docs and release notes, we should consistently use “LTS channel”.

Where LTS appears in Console (proposed surfaces)

A) Deployment Settings → Runtime
For Dedicated and (where applicable) Hosted projects.
- A “Runtime track” selector:
  - Standard (default for self-serve / non-enterprise)
  - LTS (enterprise)
- A “Pinned version” selector that changes behavior by track:
  - Standard: show recent versions with an option “Auto-upgrade within minor” (future)
  - LTS: show only LTS patches for the selected LTS line (ex: 1.18.0-lts, 1.18.1-lts, …)

B) Runtime Versions page (global view)
A listing page that helps users understand:
- What versions exist (Standard vs LTS)
- Which one they’re running
- What’s recommended
- Release notes / known issues

C) Environment / Cluster detail page (Dedicated)
If/when Dedicated clusters are surfaced individually:
- Show track + pinned version at top
- Show recent rollouts and status

D) Private deployments (Console-lite)
Reality check: many Private customers will not rely on Console for actual upgrade orchestration. They still want Console as the source-of-truth for:
- Version pin recommendation
- Release notes
- Artifact verification instructions
- Compatibility matrix and installer/Helm references

Version pinning UX details

1) Selecting an LTS line vs a patch
We need two layers:
- Choose LTS line: e.g., “Runtime 1.18 LTS” (supported through YYYY-MM-DD)
- Choose patch within line: “1.18.1-lts”

Design note:
- Customers often think in “minor” (1.18) and want to stay there.
- Patch selection should default to “Newest patch in this LTS line” but with explicit choice:
  - Toggle: “Pin to a specific patch” vs “Track latest patch in this LTS line (recommended)”
  - HOWEVER: for LTS we said stability over auto-change; some enterprise teams will reject silent patch updates.
  - Compromise option: “Track latest patch” still requires manual approval to apply (staged rollout button). See Rollout controls.

2) Explicit warnings/confirmations
When switching Standard → LTS:
- Confirmation modal text (draft copy):
  - “You’re switching to the LTS track. LTS prioritizes stability and receives security + critical fixes on a predictable cadence. Feature updates may arrive later than Standard.”
  - “Your deployment may restart during the runtime upgrade.”
  - Link: “Read LTS support & backport policy”

When switching LTS → Standard:
- Stronger warning:
  - “Standard receives frequent updates and may change performance characteristics.”
  - Suggest staying on LTS unless you need a specific feature.

When changing pinned patch within LTS:
- Display:
  - Risk/impact summary from release notes metadata (e.g., Mandatory vs Optional, “Perf: no change”, “Known issue: …”).
  - Restart note, and expected duration.

3) Showing what’s running (everywhere)
Where we show a version string, include:
- Badge: LTS / Standard
- Version: 1.18.1-lts
- Short build id: runtime build hash (first 7 chars)
- “Release notes” link (opens in new tab)
- “Known issues” link anchored to relevant section

Release notes entry points (requirements)
- The release notes link must be stable and shareable (customers paste into change tickets).
- For each LTS patch, show:
  - Summary (2–5 bullets)
  - Categories (Security, Stability/Correctness, Performance, Ops/Packaging)
  - Known issues + workarounds
  - Compatibility matrix (GPU SKUs + driver/cuda notes if relevant)
- Console should surface “Mandatory patch” if present in notes metadata.

Open question: where do release notes live?
- Option 1: Docs site URL (preferred for external)
- Option 2: Console-hosted notes (harder to keep public)
- Option 3: Both, but Console just deep-links to docs
Decision leaning: Console deep-link to docs + show a short inline summary snippet.

Rollout controls (Dedicated + Hosted)

Minimum viable controls (v1)
- “Apply update” button with:
  - Rollout to: “All” (default) or “Canary (10%)” if canary infra is ready
  - Maintenance window selector (optional; if not, just warn)
- Status: “Queued / In progress / Completed / Rolled back”
- Rollback button to previous pinned patch (if available and compatible)

What we should NOT promise in v1 UI copy
- We should not imply “zero downtime” unless runtime/SRE confirms.
- We should not imply instant rollback for Private.

Canary rollouts UX (stretch)
- For customers with multiple Dedicated pools/regions:
  - roll out per pool
  - show pool-level health (p95 latency, error rate) vs baseline
  - auto-halt criteria based on SLO dashboards (Sergio’s work)

Private deployment UX (Console as guidance)

What Private customers need visible in Console
- “Recommended LTS patch” (not auto-applied)
- “Your pinned runtime version” (from telemetry if available; otherwise user-reported)
- Download/verification section (link out):
  - checksums / signatures
  - provenance attestation
  - SBOM link if available
- Upgrade guide link and rollback checklist

Important: we must avoid making Console look like the only way to manage Private.
- Copy suggestion: “Private deployments are upgraded via installer/Helm. Use this page to choose a version and access release notes + verification materials.”

Compatibility matrix surfacing
- Show a simplified compatibility section in Console:
  - Runtime version ↔ supported GPU SKUs (A10, L4, A100, H100, etc.)
  - Minimum driver/CUDA notes where we have them
  - “Known incompatible combinations” callouts
- Full matrix lives in docs; Console shows summary + link.

Access control / eligibility
- LTS should be visible in Console only if:
  - account is Dedicated/Private OR feature flag enabled for pilot
- Users without access should see:
  - A locked “LTS” option with tooltip: “Available for Dedicated and Private plans. Contact support/sales.”

Supportability hooks (needed by Support/CS)
- In Console, add a “Copy runtime version info” button:
  - outputs: track, version, build id, region/pool, last rollout time
  - reduces back-and-forth in tickets
- Surface “Backport request” CTA (link to support form) only for LTS track.
  - Pre-fill project + version info.

Draft UI copy blocks

Track selector helper text (LTS)
“LTS receives security and critical stability fixes on a predictable cadence. Recommended for regulated or change-controlled environments.”

Pinned version helper text
“Pinning ensures your runtime doesn’t change unexpectedly. You can still choose when to apply LTS patches.”

Mandatory patch banner (if notes metadata says mandatory)
“This patch is marked Mandatory due to a security or Sev1 stability fix. Apply as soon as possible. See release notes for impact and mitigation.”

Edge cases / failure modes
- If release notes URL is unavailable, Console should:
  - still show version
  - show an error state: “Release notes unavailable. Try again or contact Support.”
- If telemetry doesn’t report exact runtime patch, only “1.18 LTS line”:
  - show “1.18.x-lts (exact patch unknown)” and link to instructions for verifying on cluster

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Auto-update semantics within LTS line
- Do we allow “track latest patch” + scheduled apply? Or only explicit pin-to-patch?
- Enterprise expectation (from early calls): no silent updates. My recommendation: require explicit apply action; allow “notify me when new patch available”.

2) How we represent support window in UI
- For each LTS line show:
  - “Supported until: 2026-03-31” (example)
  - “Maintenance mode after: …” (optional)

3) Naming and ordering in dropdowns
- Do we show LTS first (for enterprise accounts) or keep Standard first?
- For enterprise accounts, default dropdown to LTS if they’re already on LTS.

4) Do we allow switching LTS lines (1.18 LTS → 1.20 LTS) in Console?
- Might be a bigger upgrade; needs stronger warning + compatibility checks.
- Likely yes but gated behind “advanced” toggle.

5) Known issues presentation
- Do we embed a compact “Known issues affecting this version” block inline on the settings page?
- Support wants it visible; Product wants to avoid clutter.
- Suggest: inline summary with “View all known issues” link.

Next steps
- Align on terminology + auto-update stance (Product + Release Eng + SRE).
- Confirm what metadata we can reliably pull from release notes generator for Console snippets (Elliot + Connor).
- Define pilot UX scope for 1–3 enterprise accounts (Rachel + Support).
- Feed requirements into PM-914 and engineering tickets for Console implementation.

Notes from customer conversations (paraphrased)
- “We need something we can put in our change ticket: what changed, why it matters, and how to roll back.”
- “Don’t auto-upgrade us. We do monthly windows; security hotfixes are exceptions.”
- “We want the checksums and attestation linked next to the version. Make it impossible to miss.”
